articles.title: Hickory Ridge Gets $850 for Pet Adoption Fair
articles.deck: The money will be spent over the next year, with the first work starting in June.
body: The Hickory Ridge Improvement Group will post updates on its bulletin board outside the library.

The group has raised $850 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food. Beatrice Rasmussen, who has lived in Hickory Ridge for 20 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected.
The plan calls for pet adoption fair along Yardley Terrace, with work expected to start in June. Organizers say the project is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Saturday mornings.

articles.title: Letters: Juniper Street Parking Is Out of Control
body: To the editor: I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the March meeting. Please keep the accessible ramp in the budget. Many of us on Juniper Street use it every week.
Thank you for printing this letter, and for all the work the paper does to keep us informed.

To the editor: I have lived on Juniper Street for 14 years, and I want to say what a difference the Cedar Hollow Garden Club has made. I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the March meeting.
Denise Szabo, Kettle Hill
